extension: Matched CPU operating points and historical YOLO baselines
prior_exposure: A/B/C/D/E test results were public before this extension. Validation alone selects new checkpoints, operating thresholds and the speed recommendation. Test is a previously inspected benchmark.

native_deployment_paths.yolov5s: original v7.0 anchor-based objectness times class, dense + classwise NMS

data.initialization: COCO publisher weights; copy matching tensors to a six-class model

training: Same epoch/image order, augmentation, optimizer, schedule, AMP, checkpoint selection and classwise evaluation as the original study. Each model uses its native detection loss. YOLOv5s uses the published three anchor groups and the v7.0 loss gains scaled to six classes and 480 pixels.
threshold: For each checkpoint, runtime and head at 480, maximize macro recall at IoU 0.50 over validation score groups subject to at most 36 FP in 360 images. Ties prefer fewer FP, then higher cutoff. Score floor 0.001, cap 300. Freeze before opening test prediction files for that analysis.

timing.primary: decoded grayscale image to final boxes including preprocessing, synchronous forward, score thresholding and any NMS
timing.statistic: median of three within-run p95s; arithmetic mean across paired training seeds
timing.conditions: AC power, fixed affinity on four performance cores, no concurrent model training

family_selection: Report both the speed-only order and the fastest supported baseline at 480 on the default path. Qualify on validation against stock YOLO26n at independently fitted cutoffs using the original limits: no more than 1 percentage point loss in mAP50-95 or 2 points loss in any class recall, on both seed 0 and the paired three-seed mean. Use fresh validation pipeline p95 to order eligible models. Report per-seed ranks and overlapping session ranges; do not assert a uniquely faster family when ranges overlap. Evaluate on test without choosing again.
scope: The new v8n and original v5s are historical comparators at 480. The existing 256/320/480/640 sweep applies to A-E. PConv and learned fusion use the original four-cell factorial design.
